LiverDCP manuscript submitted!
Aug 8, 2026

One of the group’s major works was submitted. Here, we introduce a graph- and omics-based disease model, LiverDCP, an HGNN framework that integrates single-cell multi-omics, protein interaction networks, and structural biology to learn disease- and cell-contextualized protein representations. The framework connects systems-level disease biology with genetic risk and therapeutic target discovery, opening new opportunities for understanding liver diseases and identifying potential drug targets. Read more here.

Congratulations to the team on reaching this milestone! 🎉

Paper Accepted in Nature Communications
Mar 13, 2026

Our E. coli paper was accepted in Nature Communications. We developed an integrative framework that combines structural modeling (PrePPI), protein language models (Topsy-Turvy), and evolutionary information (ZEPPI) to predict PPIs at the proteome scale. Applying this framework to E. coli proteome, we identified hundreds of functionally coherent subnetworks — without using functional annotations, the model reveals meaningful biological predictions, enabling functional annotation for previously uncharacterized proteins. Read more here. 🥂

Collabration Paper Published
Feb 1, 2025

Our first collabration paper at UTMB was published. Dr. Zhao helped Dr. Sheng Zhang’s group at UT Health with the free energy calculation for the huntingtin HTT and Hap40 proteins. Through the hybrid structural and functional studies of the fly and human HTT-HAP40 complexes, this work demonstrated that structural similarity underlies the functional conservation of the two complexes in these evolutionarily distant species.
